feat(smoke): add standalone smoke workflows using native gh-aw-detection flag (#567)

Recompile the base smoke workflows with gh-aw v0.82.14 and add
smoke-{copilot,claude,codex}-standalone.md. The standalone workflows enable
the native external detector path (`features: gh-aw-detection: true`), which
downloads the published threat-detect binary from github/gh-aw-threat-detection
releases and runs it under AWF. This replaces the brittle
create-threat-detection-sibling-workflows.py container hack with a
first-class gh-aw frontmatter flag.

Co-authored-by: GitHub Ace <githubnext@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+---
+description: Smoke test workflow that validates Codex engine execution with the released threat-detect binary
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  schedule: daily
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+  actions: read
+name: Smoke Codex Standalone
+engine: codex
+strict: false
+features:
+  gh-aw-detection: true
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - github
+tools:
+  bash:
+    - "*"
+  github:
+  web-fetch:
+runtimes:
+  go:
+    version: "1.26"
+checkout:
+  fetch-depth: 1
+safe-outputs:
+  allowed-domains: [default-safe-outputs]
+  threat-detection:
+    continue-on-error: false
+  create-issue:
+    expires: 2h
+    close-older-issues: true
+    close-older-key: "smoke-codex-standalone"
+    labels: [automation, testing]
+timeout-minutes: 15
+---
+
+# Smoke Test: Codex Engine Validation (Standalone Detector)
+
+Keep outputs concise.
+
+This workflow validates the Codex engine while exercising the **native external
+threat-detect path** (`features: gh-aw-detection: true`). gh-aw downloads the
+published `threat-detect` binary from the `github/gh-aw-threat-detection` releases
+and runs it under AWF, replacing the script-generated container sibling.
+
+## Test Requirements
+
+1. Use GitHub tools to read the latest 2 pull requests in `${{ github.repository }}` and record their numbers and titles only.
+2. Use `web-fetch` to fetch `https://github.com/github/gh-aw-threat-detection` and verify the response mentions `gh-aw-threat-detection`.
+3. Use bash to run `make lint` and `make build` in `${{ github.workspace }}` and verify both succeed.
+4. Use bash to create a minimal artifacts directory under `/tmp/gh-aw/smoke-codex-standalone-${{ github.run_id }}` with:
+   - `aw-prompts/prompt.txt`
+   - `agent_output.json`
+5. Use bash to run `./bin/threat-detect --version` and verify it prints a version.
+6. Use bash to write a concise status file at `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/smoke-codex-standalone-${{ github.run_id }}.txt`.
+
+## Output
+
+Always create an issue titled `Smoke Test: Codex Standalone - ${{ github.run_id }}` with:
+- ✅ or ❌ for each test
+- Overall status: PASS or FAIL
+- Run URL: `${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}`
+- Timestamp

commits.message:
fix(smoke): use gh-proxy mode for GitHub tools in standalone smokes (#608)

* fix(smoke): use gh-proxy mode for GitHub tools in standalone smokes

The standalone smoke agent jobs failed Test Requirement 1 ("read the
latest 2 pull requests") because the local Docker GitHub MCP server tool
surface was not reaching the agent ("No such tool available") and the
bash `gh` fallback was unauthenticated (issues #602, #579; same pattern
as non-standalone #581).

Switch tools.github to `mode: gh-proxy`, which uses the pre-authenticated
`gh` CLI via the AWF cli-proxy sidecar instead of the local MCP server.
The proxy authenticates from GH_AW_GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_TOKEN ||
GH_AW_GITHUB_TOKEN || GITHUB_TOKEN, so it works with the default
GITHUB_TOKEN (which already has pull-requests: read), removing both the
MCP-server startup dependency and the unauthenticated-gh failure.

This is independent of the threat-detect binary version pin (v0.2.2 vs
v0.3.0), which only affects the separate detection job.

Recompiled the three *-standalone.lock.yml files.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(smoke): recompile standalone smokes without strict override

The previous recompile inadvertently baked strict:true into the lock
files, contradicting the source frontmatter's strict:false. Recompile
honoring the declared strict:false so the generated artifacts match the
documented source configuration (addresses PR review feedback).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
